section_1.title: The Digital Fingerprint: Hash Functions (1 min)
section_1.content: Introduce Cryptographic Hash Functions (SHA-256). Explain that a hash function takes any input and turns it into a fixed-length string of characters. Key concept: It is a 'one-way' street—easy to calculate but impossible to reverse.
section_1.example: Visualize a digital meat grinder: If you put a cat in, you get a unique 64-character code. If you change even one whisker on the cat, the code changes entirely, illustrating the 'avalanche effect'.

section_2.title: Digital Signatures: Asymmetric Cryptography (1.5 min)
section_2.content: Explain Public-Key Infrastructure (PKI). Introduce the concept of a Key Pair: a Private Key (your digital secret) and a Public Key (your digital address). Math concept: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) creates a relationship where the public key can verify the private key without revealing it.
section_2.example: Imagine a magical lockbox: You give out millions of copies of your open padlock (Public Key). When you use your secret key (Private Key) to sign a message, anyone with the padlock can verify it was you, but they can't open your vault.

section_3.title: Proof of Work: The Mathematical Lottery (1.5 min)
section_3.content: Explain how Bitcoin miners compete. They must find a 'nonce' (a random number) that, when hashed with transaction data, produces a result starting with a specific number of zeros. It’s a computationally expensive trial-and-error game.
section_3.example: Imagine a forest of robotic squirrels. The network sets a rule: 'Find a nut that makes the scale weigh exactly 5 grams.' Thousands of squirrels race to try different nuts. The first one to succeed announces it, and the others verify it instantly.

section_4.title: The Immutable Chain: Blockchain Integration (1 min)
section_4.content: Synthesize the previous concepts. Explain how each block contains the hash of the *previous* block. This creates a mathematical link where altering one block invalidates the entire chain, ensuring global security.
section_4.example: Visualize a stack of LEGO bricks where each new brick contains a tiny picture of the previous one. If you try to swap an old brick, the 'picture' inside the next one no longer matches, and the whole tower turns red, signaling a tamper attempt.

outline.content: Introduce Cryptographic Hash Functions (SHA-256). Explain that a hash function takes any input and turns it into a fixed-length string of characters. Key concept: It is a 'one-way' street—easy to calculate but impossible to reverse.
outline.example: Visualize a digital meat grinder: If you put a cat in, you get a unique 64-character code. If you change even one whisker on the cat, the code changes entirely, illustrating the 'avalanche effect'.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Hash functions take input to fixed-length strings.",
            "They are one-way streets, impossible to reverse.",
            "Changing input triggers the avalanche effect."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Digital Fingerprint: Hash Functions", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        input_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color="#FFFFFF").set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        input_label = Text("Data Input", font_size=18)
        input_group = VGroup(input_box, input_label)
        
        hash_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FFD700").set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.3)
        hash_label = Text("SHA-256", font_size=16)
        hash_group = VGroup(hash_circle, hash_label)
        
        output_box = Rectangle(width=3, height=0.5, color="#00FF00").set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        output_label = Text("Hash Output", font_size=18)
        output_group = VGroup(output_box, output_label)
        
        # Positioning
        self.place_at_grid(input_group, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(hash_group, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(output_group, 'D2')
        
        arrow1 = Arrow(input_group.get_right(), hash_group.get_left(), buff=0.1)
        arrow2 = Arrow(hash_group.get_right(), output_group.get_left(), buff=0.1)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(input_group), Create(hash_group), Create(arrow1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(output_group), Create(arrow2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        output_text = Text("a1b2c3d4...", font_size=20, color=WHITE).move_to(output_box)
        self.play(Write(output_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)
